labels.label: possibly

evidence.quote: Diagnosis of primary or recurrent, localized or metastatic (American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th Edition stages I-IV) head and neck cancer.
Measurable disease within the head and/or neck clinically and/or on imaging studies
More than 1 prior radiation treatment course directed to the treatment area over the patient's lifetime.

labels.note: Palliative H&N radiotherapy open to metastatic NPC after one RT course in 2022; whether he has disease in the head/neck (vs liver and bone only) is not stated.

labels.label: excluded

evidence.quote: Participants with hepatitis B (hepatitis B virus surface antigen [HbsAg] positive)
head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) of the oral cavity, hypopharynx, oropharynx, nasopharynx, larynx and sinonasal tract
Participants must have progressed following, are intolerant of, or have no available standard-of-care therapy.

labels.note: Includes nasopharyngeal primaries and he fits the line limits, but HBsAg-positive hepatitis B is listed as excluded (mis-sectioned exclusion); he is an HBV carrier on entecavir.

labels.label: not_relevant

evidence.quote: The eligible HNSCC primary tumor locations are oropharynx, oral cavity, hypopharynx, and larynx.

labels.note: HNSCC cohorts exclude nasopharynx; the other cohorts are colorectal.

labels.label: not_relevant

evidence.quote: Patients with pathologically proven diagnosis of lateralized OPC (tonsil, tongue base, soft palate, or pharyngeal wall) not involving or crossing midline.

labels.note: Definitive RT for lateralized oropharyngeal cancer; he has metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

labels.label: not_relevant

evidence.quote: Histological or cytological evidence of squamous cell carcinoma of a head and neck primary site (per American Joint Committee on Cancer [AJCC], other than nasopharynx or cuSCC).
